thread.title: Twitter reportedly blocks Alex Jones from tweeting

author: morningstar.com
title: Twitter reportedly blocks Alex Jones from tweeting
text:
By Mike Murphy
Conspiracy theorist was booted from most major platforms last week
Twitter Inc. has blocked right-wing conspiracy theorist Alex Jones from tweeting for a week, according to reports Tuesday night.
According to multiple reports, Jones's personal account was placed in read-only mode for seven days, apparently over a video urging his followers to get their weapons ready. While not a suspension, which would keep him off Twitter entirely, the move does not allow him to post tweets or retweet, like or comment on others' tweets. Jones has about 889,000 Twitter followers.
A Twitter spokesperson did not immediately respond for comment. It was unclear why Jones's account was placed in read-only mode instead of suspended.
Last week, Jones's Infowars content was removed (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/facebook-removes-infowars-pages-following-apple-and-spotify-2018-08-06) from a number of major platforms, including Facebook Inc. (FB) and Alphabet Inc.'s (GOOGL) (GOOGL) YouTube, as well as Spotify (SPOT) and Apple Inc.'s (AAPL) podcasts. The companies cited violations of their terms of service against hate speech, harassment and violent content. Twitter Chief Executive Jack Dorsey said last week (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/dorsey-says-alex-jones-isnt-blocked-from-twitter-because-he-hasnt-broken-rules-2018-08-07)that his company did not suspend him because Jones had not broken any of its rules..
A Buzzfeed reporter tweeted (https://twitter.com/RMac18/status/1029521949590835200)Tuesday night that the tweet that got Jones into trouble with Twitter linked to a video on Periscope, which Twitter owns. While Jones apparently took down the post, Media Matters saved a copy (https://www.mediamatters.org/video/2018/08/14/pericope-alex-jones-tells-supporters-get-their-battle-rifles-ready-against-antifa-mainstream-media/220995), in which Jones calls on his followers to prepare for violence. In the video, Jones urges his supporters to get "battle rifles" ready to fight "antifa," the mainstream media and "Chicom operatives."
Twitter has faced blistering criticism for years over its inability to crack down on harassment and violent speech, as well as for its role in spreading misinformation. The company has said on a number of occasions that it was working to curb abusive behavior on its service, including in May, when it announced actions against "troll-like behavior," (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/twitter-to-crack-down-on-trolls-by-demoting-their-tweets-automatically-2018-05-16) as well as a bot purge in July (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/who-lost-the-most-followers-in-twitters-sweeping-bot-purge-twitter-2018-08-01).
Twitter stock (TWTR) is up 37% year to date, compared to the S&P 500's 6% gain.
-Mike Murphy; 14-18 2233ET
